nodes.excerpt: The model can extend the harness at runtime: install npm plugins into a profile through the gated plugin_manager tool, or define session-local plugins with cordis_define — host code evaluated in a node:vm realm (5 s default bound), gone at restart. Installed host code executes in-process, outside the workspace sandbox — the project's own README says so.
nodes.label: Plugin manager + Creator mode

links.label: plugin-manager README — “installed Host code executes in-process outside the workspace sandbox”

nodes.excerpt: There is no interactive terminal UI. The primary surface is a Vite/React web app (apps/web) served by a node:http route-registration plugin on http://127.0.0.1:3080; client and host talk through a typed remote gateway. Booting dsh web composes the web-app bundle and opens the browser locally.
nodes.label: Web UI — the primary surface

nodes.excerpt: The CLI does three things: boot a named profile, manage plugins, dump config. Profiles (web, headless, sdk, sdk-minimal, acp) live under $DSH_HOME/profiles/<name>; each is a Cordis config assembled from bundle layers. Headless runs one fresh persisted session and prints the final answer.
nodes.label: CLI — profile boot, no TUI

links.label: apps/cli — profile boot, plugin management, config dump

nodes.excerpt: The Electron desktop app boots the same web profile in-process — one composition, two shells. The SDK profile serves a JSON-RPC stdio server that both the TypeScript client and the Python SDK (python/sdk) drive; both SDKs “project the loop”, so session and event changes must update both.
nodes.label: Desktop + SDKs

links.label: apps/desktop — Electron boots the web profile

nodes.excerpt: The Agent Client Protocol profile serves the composed tree over JSON-RPC stdio for editor automation. It is a deliberate subset: session/load, deletion, fork, terminals, client filesystem operations, and elicitation are explicitly unsupported. ACP clients are trusted controllers.
nodes.label: ACP server

links.label: packages/acp/acp/README.md — ACP clients are trusted controllers

nodes.excerpt: A running app is layered YAML: bundle patch files, the profile's own patch, a home-level cordis.patch.yml, --patch overlays. The base bundle alone is 95 plugin rows in 522 lines. The four modes are agent presets — plugin-list diffs: Standard vs PTC differ by exactly one row (agent-tool-presentation with mode: ptc). Rows can carry !!js conditions, so composition is platform-conditional.
nodes.label: Bundles + presets (YAML patches)

links.label: presets/ptc.patch.yml — the one row that makes PTC mode

nodes.excerpt: The fixed frame. Cordis is vendored source (upstream cordiverse/cordis packages/core @ 56b3d4f, rescoped @deepseek-ai/cordis) with 24 logged local modifications. The kernel is 2,696 lines: plugins are functions or apply(ctx, config) objects; services are context properties (ctx.llm, ctx.tools, ctx.sandbox) wired by inject/provide; every registration is an effect returning a disposer; each plugin runs as a fiber (PENDING → LOADING → ACTIVE → UNLOADING → DISPOSED).
nodes.label: Cordis runtime (vendored)

nodes.excerpt: kick() runs while (await this.turn()) {} — there is no built-in turn or step budget; a turn ends when the model stops calling tools, on abort, or when a composed plugin vetoes the agent/turn-stopping hook. Each step re-derives model context from the session log (session.deriveMessages()), executes up to 10 tool calls in parallel, and settles the streamed response back into the log as events.
nodes.label: Agent loop — ReactLoopAgent

links.label: agent-loop/src/agent.ts — kick() and the loop head
agent-loop/src/agent.ts — deriveMessages() at the step boundary
agent-loop/README.md — no built-in budget, stated plainly

nodes.excerpt: The loop never talks to a provider directly: prepareCall builds each request through the ctx.llm seam, and provider packages (the pi-ai adapter) implement it — the official DeepSeek API or bring-your-own-key providers. The seam is also where the session-log upload attaches for official-API requests.
nodes.label: LLM seam — ctx.llm

nodes.excerpt: Both guards are ordinary plugins mounted in the base bundle. timeout-policy wraps tools/execute and enforces each tool's declared timeoutMs (bash defaults to 60 s), substituting a TOOL_TIMEOUT result. repeat-tool-reminder counts consecutive identical calls and, at thresholds 3/5/8, injects a reminder into context via tools/post-execute — advisory only; it never vetoes a call.
nodes.label: Guards — timeout + reminder

nodes.excerpt: Tool packages register into a per-agent-scope effect registry. Every call passes tools/pre-execute (waterfall listeners may veto or demand approval), execution, then tools/post-execute. There is no tool search or deferred loading: in native mode every mounted tool's schema rides every request — visibility is decided at composition time, by which plugins the preset mounts. The full inventory is a generated 2,773-line catalog.
nodes.label: Tool registry — ctx.tools

links.label: base/cordis.patch.yml — the bash tool's 60 s default timeout

nodes.excerpt: A session is an append-only event log; model history, approvals, permission choices, and projections are all folds over it — the project's invariant is “model-visible ⟺ logged”. Format v4 is formally governed (finalized/released records, adjacent-only migrations in-tree). On disk: one directory per session under ~/.dsh/sessions, JSONL in checksummed zstd frames. Compaction (compaction-basic) prices each step and summarizes the oldest span into <compacted-summary> past 80% of the window.
nodes.label: Session service — the event log

nodes.excerpt: Mounted in the base bundle and enabled by default: when requests go to the official DeepSeek API, each carries a dsh_session_log field with the canonical session events since the last server-accepted watermark (≤ 8 MiB per request, at-least-once; acceptance is itself a logged event). A Settings switch pauses it — the backlog is not purged. Separately, OTel session telemetry exports only after explicit user feedback (FEEDBACK_ONLY), carrying an anonymous UUID.
nodes.label: Session-log upload + telemetry

nodes.excerpt: Providers contribute skill catalogs (filesystem directories, runtime registrations from other plugins, remote sources); the registry merges and deduplicates them. Disclosure is progressive: summaries are advertised to the model, and a skill's full body is fetched through the skill tool only when invoked. Every skill carries an invocation policy (modelInvocable / userInvocable), keeping model-facing and human-facing catalogs separate. Skills are dsh's durable, user-authored knowledge format — there is no built-in cross-session memory store.
nodes.label: Skills — ctx.skills

nodes.excerpt: Two knobs only: sandbox mode × approval policy (ask | never), bundled as named presets and pinned into the session log at creation. Under ask, an approval/request waterfall dispatches to composed answerers — and fails closed: no answerer, a throwing answerer, or an off-vocabulary answer all resolve unavailable, and the action is blocked. Approvals are one-shot; there is no “always allow”. Requests and decisions are logged (approval/asked, approval/decided) but are not model-visible. An experimental auto-review layer (off by default) can pre-decide — its reviewer sees the call, not the chain.
nodes.label: Approvals — ctx.approval

nodes.excerpt: Per-call, OS-level, fail-closed: if no backend can enforce the requested mode, the call fails with SANDBOX_UNAVAILABLE rather than running unconfined. Linux tries bubblewrap, then Landlock (a native launcher built from native/system); macOS uses Seatbelt; the Windows ACL rung reports its enforcement as partial, per call. After a denial, the model may retry once at the narrowest strictly wider mode — with a justification and a human approval, for that one call only. The project is explicit: this is same-world confinement, a guardrail for agent mistakes, not a container.
nodes.label: Sandbox — ctx.sandbox

nodes.excerpt: PTC (“Code Mode”) is a presentation transform, not a second agent: the wire surface collapses to one run_code schema plus a generated SDK, and tools.<name>(args) calls inside the model's program bridge back into the same guarded pipeline. The Node provider runs erasable TypeScript in a fresh managed process under the resolved sandbox policy; the experimental Python provider runs a CPython subprocess with no file confinement — its README says so.
nodes.label: PTC runtime — ctx.ptcRuntime

links.label: presets/ptc.patch.yml — mode: ptc on the presentation row

nodes.excerpt: dsh consumes MCP; it is not exposed by it — packages/mcp holds exactly two packages, a client and a resources bridge, and no server. Servers (stdio or Streamable HTTP) are configured one entry each, none enabled by default; their tools register as mcp__<server>__<tool>. For stdio children, the bridge strips ambient variables whose names usually identify credentials, plus all DSH_* variables, before launch. Third-party memory servers are the documented route to cross-session memory.
nodes.label: MCP client

links.label: docs/user/guide/mcp-memory.md — stdio env stripping; memory over MCP
